questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the main levers of visual hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The levers are size, weight, contrast, position and whitespace. Licensing has no visual effect.

questions.q: Which spacing value sits on the 8pt grid?
questions.explanation: 24 is 3 x 8. The others are not multiples of 8.

questions.q: What is the recommended minimum touch target size on mobile?
questions.explanation: 44 x 44px is large enough for most fingertips to tap reliably.

questions.q: How should related elements be spaced compared with unrelated ones?
options: Always separated by a divider line
questions.explanation: Proximity signals relationship, so related items should sit closer together.

questions.q: What does the squint test check?
options: Whether the font is legible at small sizes
Whether the most important element still stands out when blurred
Whether the colors work for color-blind users
Whether the layout matches the grid
questions.explanation: Blurring removes detail so only the hierarchy remains. The focal point should still be visible.

questions.q: How many primary focal points should a screen ideally have?
questions.explanation: Competing focal points weaken each other. Aim for one dominant element.

questions.q: How many typeface families are usually enough for an interface?
questions.explanation: Restraint keeps a design consistent. If you use two, make them clearly different.

questions.q: A type scale uses a 1.25 ratio and starts at 16px. What is the next size up?
What is a comfortable line length for body text?
questions.explanation: 45 to 75 characters lets the eye travel along a line and find the next one easily.

questions.q: Which line height works well for body text?
questions.explanation: 1.4 to 1.6 gives lines enough room without feeling disconnected.

questions.q: What does x-height describe?
options: The height of lowercase letters such as x, excluding ascenders
The distance between two lines of text
The thickness of a letter stroke
questions.explanation: A larger x-height generally makes a typeface feel bigger and easier to read at small sizes.

questions.q: What is the recommended minimum body text size on mobile?
questions.explanation: 16px is a widely used floor for readable mobile body text.

questions.q: What do the letters in HSL stand for?
questions.explanation: HSL describes a color by its hue, how saturated it is and how light it is.

questions.q: What does the 60-30-10 rule recommend?
questions.explanation: A calm dominant color, a supporting color and a small accent keep a layout balanced.

questions.q: Colors that sit opposite each other on the color wheel are called:
questions.explanation: Complementary pairs, like blue and orange, create the strongest contrast of hue.

questions.q: What contrast ratio does WCAG require for normal-size text?
questions.explanation: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text is the AA level.

questions.q: Why shouldn't color be the only way to show an error?
options: Some users cannot tell certain colors apart
It makes the page print slowly
There is no reason, it is only a style choice
questions.explanation: Color-blind and low-vision users may miss it. Add an icon or message as well.

questions.q: Where is the accent color best used?
questions.explanation: Saving the accent for key actions makes those actions easy to find.

questions.q: What do low-fidelity wireframes deliberately leave out?
questions.explanation: Keeping style out forces you to solve structure and priority first.

questions.q: In a user flow, which shape usually represents a yes/no decision?
questions.explanation: A diamond marks a branching decision such as 'Is the user logged in?'.

questions.q: How many columns are commonly used for a mobile layout grid?
questions.explanation: 4 columns is a common mobile pattern. Desktop usually uses 12.

questions.q: Where is the thumb zone on a phone?
options: The lower middle of the screen
questions.explanation: That area is easiest to reach one-handed, so frequent actions belong there.

questions.q: What is the 'happy path' in a user flow?
options: The route where everything goes as expected
The path with the fewest colors
The route taken after an error
questions.explanation: Map the happy path first, then add error and edge cases.

questions.q: Why start wireframing on paper before using a design tool?
options: It is fast and cheap to change and keeps focus on structure
Color is impossible to use digitally
questions.explanation: Paper removes tool friction and temptation to polish too early.

questions.q: A screen has a headline, three buttons and a banner, all the same size, weight and color. What is the best first fix?
options: Make one element clearly dominant using size, weight or contrast
questions.explanation: Hierarchy comes from difference. Choose one focal point and rank the rest below it.

questions.q: The gap between a title and its body is 13px. Which is the nearest 8pt-grid value?
questions.explanation: 13 is 3px from 16 and 5px from 8. The 8pt grid allows 8 and 16, so 16 is nearest.

questions.q: A primary button is 36px tall on a phone. What is the problem?
options: It is below the 44px touch target minimum
Nothing, buttons can be any size
questions.explanation: Small targets cause mis-taps. Raise it to at least 44px.

questions.q: A paragraph runs about 140 characters per line. What should you change?
options: Narrow the text column to 45 to 75 characters
questions.explanation: Overly long lines make it hard to find the start of the next line.

questions.q: Light grey text (#AAAAAA) sits on a white background. What is the likely issue?
questions.explanation: That pair is around 2.3:1, well below the 4.5:1 needed for normal text.

questions.q: In a wellness app, where should the 10% accent color go?
questions.explanation: The accent is for the most important action so it stands out.

questions.q: Why does this course teach hierarchy, type and color before tools?
options: Tools only execute decisions, and principles tell you which decisions to make
questions.explanation: Knowing why something works lets you use any tool well.

questions.q: On a form, labels sit nearer the previous field than their own field. What principle is broken and how do you fix it?
options: Proximity. Move each label closer to its own field than to the previous one.
questions.explanation: Distance communicates relationship. Labels must visibly belong to their fields.

questions.q: What belongs inside a decision diamond in a user flow?
options: A yes/no question such as 'Is the user logged in?'
questions.explanation: Diamonds branch the flow based on a condition.

questions.q: Which font pairing approach is generally recommended?
options: Two clearly different faces with distinct roles
A decorative face for all body text
questions.explanation: Similar-but-not-identical faces look like a mistake. Clear contrast looks deliberate.

questions.q: Which item belongs in a low-fi wireframe?
questions.explanation: Low-fi wireframes use labeled placeholders to focus on structure.

questions.q: Why include an error path in a user flow?
options: Because users will hit failures and you need to design how they recover
It is only needed in desktop apps
questions.explanation: Real journeys include failures. Planning recovery prevents dead ends.
